claim.why_it_matters: A heading nested at the wrong level breaks the section tree a clause lookup walks: 6.11.3 reads as a sibling of 6.11 instead of its child.
claim.note: Heading at the wrong level: its parent 6.11 THE DIVIDE STATEMENT is '### 6.11' on page 312 and its siblings 6.11.1/6.11.2 are '####', so 6.11.3 is rendered at the same level as its parent section instead of '####'.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page VI-81 (PDF p313) shows '6.11.3 Syntax Rules' as a subsection heading of 6.11 THE DIVIDE STATEMENT. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md the parent is '### 6.11 THE DIVIDE STATEMENT' (line 12931), siblings '#### 6.11.1 Function' and '#### 6.11.2 General Format' (12933, 12937), but '### 6.11.3 Syntax Rules' (13020) sits at the parent's level. The heading text is present; the defect is the nesting level, which places 6.11.3 as a sibling of 6.11 in the section tree. The same page also carries '6.11.4 General Rules', likewise rendered '### 6.11.4' (13028) instead of '####'. (Separately, 6.11 itself is '###' while 6.10 is '##', a page-312 matter.)
verdict.corrected_description: Heading-level defect, not a missing heading: '6.11.3 Syntax Rules' is rendered '###' (same level as its parent '### 6.11') instead of '####' like its siblings 6.11.1/6.11.2. The same defect affects '6.11.4 General Rules' on this same page ('### 6.11.4' should be '####').
